claim_1.claim: whole-genome genotyping analysis of peripheral blood genomic DNA from healthy adult male volunteers in the discovery cohort and healthy adult female volunteers in the validation cohort after influenza vaccination (day 0), integrated with serial transcript measurements, showed that multiple loci had significant cis-acting genotype-expression associations together with a transcriptional response to vaccination compared to baseline (day 0), including 78 genes that met stringent thresholds in both cohorts.

sources.quote: A majority of these (467 SNP-transcript pairs, corresponding to 78 unique genes) would pass equally stringent thresholds in both cohorts (genotype effect p<5 × 10−8, day effect p<0.01). A Manhattan plot of these results is presented in Figure 1.

comparison.finding: 467 SNP-transcript pairs corresponding to 78 unique genes passed equally stringent thresholds for cis-acting genotype-expression associations with transcriptional response to vaccination in both the discovery and validation cohorts

claim_2.claim: whole-genome genotyping analysis of peripheral blood genomic DNA from healthy adult male volunteers in the discovery cohort and healthy adult female volunteers in the validation cohort after influenza vaccination (day 0), integrated with serial transcript measurements, showed that at some loci the genetic effect on expression was enhanced or only apparent after vaccination compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: This analysis revealed multiple loci at which the genetic effect was either enhanced or only apparent after the experimental perturbation.

claim_3.claim: whole-genome genotyping analysis of peripheral blood genomic DNA from healthy adult male volunteers in the discovery cohort and healthy adult female volunteers in the validation cohort after influenza vaccination (day 0), integrated with serial transcript measurements, showed that increases in the magnitude of the genetic effect after vaccination were driven mainly by increased strength of the genotype-expression association rather than reduced within-genotype variance compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Figure 2B shows that an increase in the strength of the genotype effect (slope of the additive association) was the main driver for the observed change in Rg2, and that this amplitude change was a general feature of the loci in which we observed both a strong cis-acting eQTL and a transcriptional response to the vaccine stimulus.

claim_4.claim: whole-genome genotyping analysis of peripheral blood genomic DNA from healthy adult male volunteers in the discovery cohort and healthy adult female volunteers in the validation cohort after influenza vaccination (day 0), integrated with transcript and antibody measurements, showed that 20 loci had the strongest evidence that genetic variation influenced the humoral response to influenza vaccination compared to loci not meeting the combined genotype-expression-antibody criteria.

sources.quote: We imposed an additional selection threshold based on this correlation, and identified 20 genes that show evidence of significant genotype-expression association (genotype effect p<5 × 10−8), a significant correlation between the transcriptional and antibody responses (expression-antibody effect p<0.05), and either a transcriptional response to the vaccine (day effect p<0.01) or evidence of a change in the magnitude of the genetic effect after vaccination (top 1% of the delta-Rg2 distribution) in the two independent cohorts. These loci have the strongest evidence of genetic variation influencing the immune response to the vaccine

comparison.finding: 20 loci showed the strongest evidence across the discovery and validation cohorts that genetic variation influenced the humoral response to influenza vaccination based on combined genotype-expression-antibody criteria

claim_5.claim: whole-genome genotyping analysis of peripheral blood genomic DNA from healthy adult male volunteers in the discovery cohort and healthy adult female volunteers in the validation cohort after influenza vaccination (day 0), integrated with transcript and antibody measurements, showed that SNPs from the 20 prioritized loci were enriched for true genetic associations with antibody response compared to background SNPs from the full data set.

sources.quote: The quantile-quantile plot from the association tests performed on these SNPs shows marked deviation from the empirical null distribution for QTL associations (Figure 6), supporting the idea that these loci are enriched for true genetic associations.

comparison.finding: SNPs from the 20 prioritized loci were enriched for true genetic associations with antibody response compared to background SNPs from the full data set

claim_6.claim: whole-genome genotyping analysis of peripheral blood genomic DNA from the 20 prioritized loci in vaccinated healthy adult male and female cohorts, integrated with transcript and antibody measurements, showed that the observed genotype-expression-antibody patterns trended toward a causal model rather than a reactive model compared to the alternative reactive explanation.

sources.quote: We found that the patterns in the data trend toward the causal model compared to the reactive model (Figure 7B), but a power analysis based on the distribution of the empirical effect sizes of our observed associations also indicates that our sample size is too modest to support definitive conclusions (Figure 7C).

sources.quote: We began by identifying SNP-transcript pairs with both significant evidence of a cis-acting eQTL and significant changes in gene expression in response to vaccination.
A majority of these (467 SNP-transcript pairs, corresponding to 78 unique genes) would pass equally stringent thresholds in both cohorts (genotype effect p<5 × 10−8, day effect p<0.01).

claim_9.claim: global transcript abundance analysis of peripheral blood RNA from healthy adult male volunteers in the discovery cohort and healthy adult female volunteers in the validation cohort at days 0, 1, 3, and 14 after influenza vaccination (day 0), using content analysis of vaccine-responsive loci, showed enrichment for genes involved in membrane trafficking, antigen processing, antigen presentation, cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-mediated apoptosis of target cells, and dendritic cell maturation and function compared to the genomic background.

sources.quote: Content analysis on the union of the two sets (98 genes) showed significant enrichment for genes involved in antigen processing and presentation, cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-mediated apoptosis of target cells, dendritic cell maturation and function, and membrane trafficking (Figure 3).

claim_10.claim: global transcript abundance analysis of peripheral blood RNA from healthy adult male volunteers in the discovery cohort and healthy adult female volunteers in the validation cohort at days 0, 1, 3, and 14 after influenza vaccination (day 0), integrated with antibody measurements, showed that expression of 301 transcripts correlated with the magnitude of the antibody response compared to transcripts without such correlation.

sources.quote: In a combined analysis of the two cohorts in the present study, 301 transcripts were found to correlate with the magnitude of the antibody response (Figure 4).

claim_11.claim: global transcript abundance analysis of peripheral blood RNA from healthy adult male volunteers in the discovery cohort and healthy adult female volunteers in the validation cohort at day 1 after influenza vaccination (day 0), integrated with antibody measurements, showed that DYNLT1 expression was positively correlated with the magnitude of the antibody response compared to lower DYNLT1 expression.

sources.quote: (A) Examples of positive (DYNLT1) and negative (ANKRD33) correlation between gene expression on day 1 and the magnitude of the antibody response to the vaccine.

comparison.finding: DYNLT1 expression on day 1 was positively correlated with the magnitude of the antibody response to influenza vaccination

claim_12.claim: global transcript abundance analysis of peripheral blood RNA from healthy adult male volunteers in the discovery cohort and healthy adult female volunteers in the validation cohort at day 1 after influenza vaccination (day 0), integrated with antibody measurements, showed that ANKRD33 expression was negatively correlated with the magnitude of the antibody response compared to lower ANKRD33 expression.

claim_13.claim: hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) tests analysis of serum from healthy adult male volunteers in the discovery cohort and healthy adult female volunteers in the validation cohort at days 14 and 28 after influenza vaccination (day 0), integrated across H1N1, H3N2, and FluB responses, showed that post-vaccination antibody titer change was negatively correlated with pre-vaccination titer compared to individuals with lower baseline titers.

sources.quote: For all antigens, the change in antibody titer post-vaccination is known to be negatively correlated with the pre-vaccination titer.

comparison.finding: at day 14, post-vaccination antibody titer change was negatively correlated with pre-vaccination titer
at day 28, post-vaccination antibody titer change was negatively correlated with pre-vaccination titer
